sentences.zh: 裴滿亨

translations.literal: Pei Manheng
translations.idiomatic: Pei Manheng

sentences.zh: 裴滿亨，字仲通，本名河西，臨潢府人。

translations.literal: Pei Manheng, style name Zhongtong, original name Hexi, was a native of Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Manheng, whose style name was Zhongtong and whose original name was Hexi, came from Linhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先世居遼海，祖諱虎山者，天輔間移屯東受降城，以禦夏人，後徙居臨潢。

translations.literal: His ancestors had long lived in the Liao Sea region; his grandfather, whose taboo name was Hushan, during the Tianfu era was moved to garrison at the Eastern Surrender City to guard against the Xia, and later relocated to Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long resided in the Liao Sea area. His grandfather, known as Hushan, was transferred during the Tianfu period to garrison the Eastern Surrender City against the Western Xia and later moved to Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 亨性敦敏習儒，大定間，收充奉職，世宗謂曰：「聞爾業進士舉，其勿忘為學也。」

translations.literal: Heng was by nature earnest and quick-witted and studied the Confucian classics; during the Dading era he was enrolled as a palace attendant, and Emperor Shizong said to him: "I have heard that you are pursuing the jinshi examinations—do not forget your studies."
translations.idiomatic: Heng was earnest, quick to learn, and devoted to Confucian study. In the Dading period he was taken on as a palace attendant. Emperor Shizong told him, "I hear you are preparing for the jinshi examination—do not neglect your learning."

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢第，世宗嘉之，升為奉禦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he passed the examination; the emperor commended him and promoted him to palace attendant-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Dading he passed the examinations. The emperor praised him and promoted him to palace attendant-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 一日問以上古為治之道，亨奏：「陛下欲興唐、虞之治，要在進賢，退不肖，信賞罰，薄征斂而已。」

translations.literal: One day he was asked about the way of governing in antiquity; Heng memorialized: "If Your Majesty wishes to revive the governance of Tang and Yu, the essentials are to advance the worthy, dismiss the unworthy, trust rewards and punishments, and lighten taxes and levies—nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: One day he was asked about ancient principles of governance. Heng replied, "If Your Majesty wishes to restore the rule of the age of Tang and Yu, you need only advance the worthy, remove the unworthy, make rewards and punishments credible, and keep taxes and levies light."

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，諭之曰：「朕左右侍臣多以門第顯，惟爾由科甲進，且先朝信臣，國家利害，為朕盡言。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, he instructed him: "Most of the attendants at my side have risen through noble birth; you alone advanced through the civil examinations, and you are moreover a trusted minister of the former reign—speak fully to me on what helps or harms the state."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhangzong succeeded to the throne, he told him, "Most of those around me rose by family rank alone; you came up through the examinations and were trusted by the previous emperor. Tell me plainly whatever affects the welfare of the state."

sentences.zh: 俄擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 內侍梁道兒恃恩驕橫，朝士側目，亨劾奏其奸。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Liang Dao'er relied on favor and was arrogant and overbearing; court officials looked askance at him, and Heng impeached and reported his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant Liang Dao'er abused imperial favor and behaved arrogantly; officials shrank from him, and Heng memorialized against his misconduct.

sentences.zh: 遷鎬王府尉，出為定國軍節度副使，三遷同知大名府事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commandant of the Prince of Hao's household, then sent out as deputy military commissioner of the Dingguo Army, and after three promotions became associate prefect of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became commandant of the Prince of Hao's household, then left the capital as deputy military commissioner of the Dingguo Army, and after three further promotions served as associate prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 先是，豪猾從衡，前政莫制，亨下車宣明約束，闔境帖然。

translations.literal: Previously powerful ruffians had run rampant and prior administrations could not control them; when Heng took office he proclaimed regulations clearly, and the whole circuit became tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Before his arrival, powerful local bullies had run unchecked and no prior administration could restrain them. As soon as Heng took office he proclaimed clear regulations, and the entire jurisdiction settled down.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，改河南路按察副使，就遷本路副統軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was changed to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Henan Circuit and was then promoted in that circuit to deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was made deputy surveillance commissioner of the Henan Circuit and soon afterward promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 中都、西京等路按察使。

translations.literal: [He became] surveillance commissioner of the Zhongdu, Xijing, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed surveillance commissioner for the Zhongdu, Xijing, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 時世襲家豪奪民田，亨檢其實，悉還正之。

translations.literal: At the time hereditary great houses seized commoners' fields by force; Heng investigated the facts and restored them all to their rightful owners.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary magnates were seizing commoners' land by force. Heng verified each case and returned the fields to their rightful owners.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年，改安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was transferred to military commissioner of the Anwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he was made military commissioner of the Anwu Army.

sentences.zh: 歲大雪，民多凍殍，亨輸己俸為之周贍，及勸率僚屬大姓同出物以濟。

translations.literal: That year heavy snow fell and many people froze to death; Heng contributed his own salary to relieve them and urged his subordinates and great clans to donate goods together for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow that year left many dead of exposure. Heng gave his own salary for relief and urged his staff and leading families to contribute supplies as well.

sentences.zh: 轉河東南北路按察使，卒於官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Hedong North and South circuits and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Hedong North and South circuits and died in office.

sentences.zh: 上聞而惜之，贈嘉議大夫，賻物甚厚。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he regretted his loss, posthumously enfeoffed him as Jiayi Grand Master, and granted very generous funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned his loss, posthumously enfeoffed him as Jiayi Grand Master, and granted unusually generous funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 亨性尤謹密，出入宮禁數年，讜議忠言多所裨益，有稿則焚之，雖家人輩莫知也。

translations.literal: Heng was especially discreet; for several years entering and leaving the palace precincts, his forthright loyal counsel was of much benefit, and when he had drafts he burned them—even his own family did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was exceptionally discreet. During his years in and out of the palace, his candid loyal counsel proved of great benefit; he burned any draft he made, so that even his household never knew what he had said.

sentences.zh: 所曆州郡，皆有政績可紀雲。

translations.literal: In every prefecture and circuit he served there were administrative achievements worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: In every prefecture and circuit he held office, his achievements were worth recording.

sentences.zh: 斡勒忠

translations.literal: Wala Zhong
translations.idiomatic: Wala Zhong

sentences.zh: 斡勒忠，本名宋浦，蓋州人也。

translations.literal: Wala Zhong, original name Song Pu, was a native of Gaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wala Zhong, whose original name was Song Pu, came from Gaizhou.

sentences.zh: 習女直、契丹字，曆兵部、樞密院、尚書省令史，再轉大理寺知法，遷右三部司正。

translations.literal: He studied Jurchen and Khitan script, served successively as clerk in the Ministry of War, the Bureau of Military Affairs, and the Secretariat, was twice transferred to legal specialist of the Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted to director of the Right Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Jurchen and Khitan script, served as a clerk in the Ministry of War, the Bureau of Military Affairs, and the Secretariat, was twice transferred to legal specialist at the Court of Judicial Review, and rose to director of the Right Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 練達邊事，嘗奉命使北，歸致馬四千餘匹，詔褒諭之。

translations.literal: Skilled in frontier affairs, he was once ordered on embassy to the north; on his return he presented more than four thousand horses, and an edict praised and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in frontier affairs, he was once sent on embassy to the north and returned with more than four thousand horses; an edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 大定二十六年，為監察御史，轉尚書省都事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Dading he became investigating censor and was transferred to chief clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Dading he became investigating censor, then chief clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 章宗立，遷尚書兵部員外郎，出為滄州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of War in the Secretariat and sent out as prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong succeeded, he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of War in the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 河東路提刑副使徒單移刺古舉以自代，改滕州刺史。

translations.literal: Tudan Yilagua, deputy chief judicial commissioner of the Hedong Circuit, recommended him to succeed himself, and he was changed to prefect of Tengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yilagua, deputy chief judicial commissioner of the Hedong Circuit, recommended Zhong to succeed him, and Zhong was made prefect of Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗調發黃河船，數以稽期聽贖。

translations.literal: He had once requisitioned Yellow River boats and several times, for missing deadlines, was allowed to redeem the penalty with payment.
translations.idiomatic: He had once requisitioned Yellow River transport boats and, when deadlines were missed, was repeatedly allowed to pay fines in lieu of punishment.

sentences.zh: 授北京副留守，入為同簽樞密院事，兼沂王傅。

translations.literal: He was appointed deputy guardian of the Northern Capital, entered the capital as associate privy councilor, and concurrently tutor to the Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed deputy guardian of the Northern Capital, then entered the capital as associate privy councilor and concurrent tutor to the Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，拜武甯軍節度使，致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an he was appointed military commissioner of the Wuning Army and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an he was appointed military commissioner of the Wuning Army and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Taihe, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Taihe at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 忠性敦愨，通法律，以直自守，不交權貴，故時譽歸之。

translations.literal: Zhong was by nature honest and sincere, understood the law, upheld integrity, and did not associate with the powerful—hence contemporary reputation went to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was honest and sincere by nature, versed in law, and upheld integrity without courting the powerful; for this his contemporaries held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 張大節

translations.literal: Zhang Dajie
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dajie

sentences.zh: 張大節，字信之，代州五台人。

translations.literal: Zhang Dajie, style name Xinzhi, was a native of Wutai in Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dajie, whose style name was Xinzhi, came from Wutai in Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢天德三年進士第，調崞縣丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Tiande and was appointed assistant magistrate of Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Tiande and was appointed assistant magistrate of Guo County.

sentences.zh: 改東京市令。

translations.literal: He was changed to market superintendent of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made market superintendent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗判留務，甚愛重之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong judged retained duties he greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong handled retained duties at court, he held Dajie in high regard.

sentences.zh: 海陵修汴京，以大節領其役。

translations.literal: When Prince Hailing repaired Bianjing, Dajie directed that project.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hailing rebuilt Bianjing, Dajie was put in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 世宗改元於遼東，或勸赴之，富貴可一朝遂，大節曰：「自有定分，何遽爾。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong changed the reign title in Liaodong, some urged him to go join him, saying wealth and honor could be secured in a morning; Dajie said: "Each has his allotted portion—why be in such haste?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong changed the reign title in Liaodong, some urged Dajie to go join him, promising rank and riches overnight. Dajie said, "Fortune has its fixed allotment—why rush like that?"

sentences.zh: 隨例補尚書省令史，擢秘書郎、大理司直。

translations.literal: He followed precedent to fill a clerkship in the Secretariat and was promoted to secretary and direct judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He took up a clerkship in the Secretariat by routine appointment and was promoted to secretary and direct judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 會左警巡使闕，世宗謂宰臣曰：「朕得其人矣。」

translations.literal: When the post of left metropolitan patrol was vacant, Emperor Shizong told the chief ministers: "I have my man."
translations.idiomatic: When the post of left metropolitan patrol fell vacant, Shizong told his chief ministers, "I have found the right man."

sentences.zh: 遂授大節。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed Dajie.
translations.idiomatic: He promptly appointed Dajie to the post.

sentences.zh: 俄以杖殺豪民為有司所劾，削一階解職。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for beating a powerful local to death, he was impeached by the authorities, demoted one rank, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was impeached by the authorities for beating a powerful local bully to death, demoted one rank, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授同知洺州防禦使事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed associate commissioner of the Luozhou Defense Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed associate commissioner of the Luozhou Defense Army.

sentences.zh: 入為太府丞、工部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 盧溝水齧安次，承詔護視堤城。

translations.literal: The Lugou River eroded An'ci; he received an edict to oversee the dikes and walls.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lugou River undermined An'ci, he received orders to supervise the dikes and fortifications.

sentences.zh: 擢修內司使，推排東京路戶藉，人服其平。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commissioner of the Directorate of Palace Repairs and conducted household registration surveys on the Eastern Capital circuit; people accepted his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to commissioner of the Directorate of Palace Repairs, he surveyed household registers on the Eastern Capital circuit, and the people accepted his fairness.

sentences.zh: 進工部郎中。

translations.literal: He advanced to director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 時阜通監鑄錢法弊，與吏部員外郎麻珪蒞其事。

translations.literal: At the time the coinage law of the Funtong Directorate was defective; together with Vice Director Ma Gui of the Ministry of Personnel he went to rectify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Funtong Directorate's coinage regulations were defective; together with Ma Gui, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, he was sent to handle the matter.

sentences.zh: 積銅皆窳惡，或欲征民先所給直，大節曰：「此有司受納之過，民何與焉。」

translations.literal: The accumulated copper was all inferior; some wished to levy from the people the price previously paid; Dajie said: "This is the fault of the officials who received it—what have the people to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: The stockpiled copper was all substandard, and some proposed recovering from the people what they had been paid. Dajie said, "That is the fault of the receiving officials—what offense have the people committed?"

sentences.zh: 以其事聞，卒得免征。

translations.literal: He reported the matter upward and in the end the levy was not imposed.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the matter to the throne, and in the end the levy was waived.

sentences.zh: 就改戶部郎中，定襄退吏誣縣民匿銅者十八村，大節廉得其實，抵吏罪，民斫石頌之。

translations.literal: He was then changed to director of the Ministry of Revenue; a retired clerk of Dingxiang falsely accused villagers of eighteen hamlets of hoarding copper; Dajie investigated and learned the truth, punished the clerk, and the people carved stone to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made director of the Ministry of Revenue. A retired clerk in Dingxiang falsely accused villagers in eighteen hamlets of hoarding copper; Dajie investigated, found the truth, punished the clerk, and the people carved a stone inscription in his praise.

sentences.zh: 召授工部侍郎，改戶部。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed vice minister of Works, then changed to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed vice minister of Works, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗東巡，徙太府監，諭之曰：「侍郎與太府監品同，以從行支應籍卿辦耳。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong toured the east, he was moved to director of the Imperial Treasury; the emperor instructed him: "The vice minister and the director of the Imperial Treasury are of equal rank—this is only so you may handle supplies for the journey."
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong toured the east, Dajie was made director of the Imperial Treasury. The emperor told him, "A vice minister and the director of the Imperial Treasury are equal in rank—I am only shifting you so you can manage supplies for the journey."

sentences.zh: 尋為宋生日使，還授橫海軍節度使，過闕謁謝東宮，顯宗撫慰良久，曰：「萬事惟中可也。」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he served as birthday envoy to Song; on his return he was appointed military commissioner of the Henghai Army; passing the capital he paid respects at the Eastern Palace, and Emperor Xianzong comforted him at length, saying: "In all matters, moderation will do."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as birthday envoy to Song. On his return he was appointed military commissioner of the Henghai Army. When he passed the capital to pay his respects at the Eastern Palace, Emperor Xianzong comforted him at length and said, "In all things, the middle way is enough."

sentences.zh: 因榜其公堂曰「惟中」。

translations.literal: He therefore posted on his public hall the words "Moderation Alone."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore posted the words "Moderation Alone" in his public hall.

sentences.zh: 郡境有巨盜久不獲，大節以方略擒之。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture there was a great bandit long uncaptured; Dajie took him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: A major bandit in the prefecture had long evaded capture; Dajie seized him by strategy.

sentences.zh: 後河決于衛，橫流而東，滄境有九河故道，大節即相宜繕堤，水不為害。

translations.literal: Later the Yellow River broke its banks at Wei and flowed east across the land; within Cangzhou were the old courses of the Nine Rivers; Dajie promptly repaired dikes where appropriate, and the water did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Yellow River burst its banks at Wei and flowed east in flood; Cangzhou still had the old channels of the Nine Rivers. Dajie repaired the dikes where needed, and the waters did no damage.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，擢中都路都轉運使，因言河東賦重宜減，議者或不同，大節以他路田賦質之，遂命減焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, he was promoted to director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit; he said the land tax in Hedong was heavy and ought to be reduced—some in council disagreed, but Dajie compared it with the field tax of other circuits, and an order to reduce it was issued.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong succeeded, Dajie was made director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit. He argued that Hedong's land tax was too heavy and should be reduced; some officials disagreed, but Dajie compared it with field taxes in other circuits, and a reduction was ordered.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕，不許，徙知太原府，以並、代鄉郡，故優寵之。

translations.literal: He requested retirement but was not permitted; he was moved to prefect of Taiyuan, and because Bing and Dai were his native circuits he was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire but was refused and was instead made prefect of Taiyuan; because Bing and Dai were his home region, he received special favor.

sentences.zh: 近郭有男子被殺者，聞其妻哭聲不哀，召而審之，果為姦夫所殺，人以為神。

translations.literal: Near the city a man was murdered; hearing that his wife's weeping was not mournful, he summoned and examined her, and it turned out she had been killed by her lover—the people regarded it as divine.
translations.idiomatic: A man was murdered near the city wall. Hearing that the wife's weeping was not truly mournful, he summoned and questioned her and found she had been killed by her lover; people called it uncanny insight.

sentences.zh: 西山有晉叔虞祠，舊以施錢輸公使庫，大節還其廟以給營繕。

translations.literal: On the western hills was the shrine of Shuyu of Jin; formerly the donated money was sent to the public envoy treasury; Dajie returned it to the temple for repairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the western hills stood the shrine of Jin Prince Shuyu; offerings had been diverted to the public envoy treasury. Dajie restored the funds to the shrine for its upkeep.

sentences.zh: 選授河東路提刑使，未赴，留知大興府事，治有能名。

translations.literal: He was selected and appointed chief judicial commissioner of the Hedong Circuit but had not yet gone when he was retained to govern Daxing Prefecture, and his administration won a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as chief judicial commissioner of the Hedong Circuit, he had not yet departed when he was kept on to govern Daxing Prefecture, where his administration gained a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 閱歲，移知廣寧府，複請老，授震武軍節度使。

translations.literal: After a year he was moved to govern Guangning Prefecture, again requested old age leave, and was appointed military commissioner of the Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was transferred to Guangning Prefecture, again sought retirement, and was appointed military commissioner of the Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 部有銀冶，有司以為爭盜由此生，付河東、西京提刑司與州同議，皆以官榷為便，大節曰：「山澤之利，當與民共，且貧而無業者，雖嚴刑能禁其竊取乎？

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction was a silver smeltery; the authorities thought strife and banditry arose from this and referred it to the Hedong and Xijing judicial commissioners to discuss with the prefecture; all thought state monopoly convenient; Dajie said: "The profit of mountains and marshes should be shared with the people, and besides, for the poor without livelihood, can severe punishments stop secret mining?
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction had a silver works. Officials believed theft and strife arose from it and referred the matter to the Hedong and Xijing judicial commissioners and the prefecture; all favored state monopoly. Dajie said, "The bounty of hills and marshes should be shared with the people. Besides, for the poor without livelihood, can harsh punishments stop secret mining?

sentences.zh: 宜明諭民，授地輸課，則其遊手者有所資，於官亦便。」

translations.literal: It is fitting clearly to instruct the people, grant land, and collect dues—then idlers will have support, and it will also be convenient for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Better to explain the policy clearly, grant plots, and collect dues—then idle hands will have a livelihood, and the state will benefit as well."

sentences.zh: 上從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 複乞致仕，許之，仍擢其子尚書刑部員外郎岩叟為忻州刺史，以便祿養。

translations.literal: He again requested retirement and was permitted; his son Yansou, vice director of the Ministry of Punishments in the Secretariat, was also promoted to prefect of Xinzhou so he might conveniently support his father.
translations.idiomatic: He again sought retirement and was granted it. His son Yansou, vice director in the Ministry of Punishments, was also made prefect of Xinzhou so he could support his father nearby.

sentences.zh: 承安五年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Cheng'an, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Cheng'an at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 大節素廉勤好學，能勵勉後進，自以得學于任倜，待倜子如親而加厚。

translations.literal: Dajie was by nature frugal, diligent, and fond of learning, able to encourage later generations; he considered himself indebted to Ren Chou for his learning and treated Chou's son as kin with added kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Dajie was frugal, diligent, and devoted to learning, and he encouraged younger scholars. He regarded himself as Ren Chou's student and treated Chou's son with the kindness due to family.

sentences.zh: 又善弈棋，當世推為第一，嘗被召與禮部尚書張景仁弈。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at weiqi, ranked first in his day, and was once summoned to play with Zhang Jingren, minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at weiqi and was ranked first in his age; he was once summoned to play with Zhang Jingren, minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗謂宰臣曰：「人多稱王翛能官，以朕觀之，凡事不肯盡心，一老奸耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once told the chief ministers: "Many praise Wang Xiao as able in office, but in my view he is unwilling to give his full effort in anything—nothing but an old schemer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong once told his chief ministers, "Many praise Wang Xiao as an able official, but as I see it he never gives his full effort to anything—he is only an old schemer.

sentences.zh: 張大節賦性剛直，果于從政，遠在王翛之上，惜乎用之太晚。」

translations.literal: Zhang Dajie is by nature upright and firm and resolute in government—far above Wang Xiao; it is a pity he was employed too late."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dajie is upright by nature and resolute in administration—far above Wang Xiao. It is a pity he was used too late."

sentences.zh: 又屢語近臣曰：「某某非不幹，然不及張大節忠實也。」

translations.literal: He also repeatedly told close ministers: "So-and-so is not unwilling to act, yet he does not equal Zhang Dajie's loyalty and honesty."
translations.idiomatic: He also told close ministers more than once, "So-and-so is not unwilling to serve, yet none equals Zhang Dajie's loyalty and honesty."

sentences.zh: 其見知如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 子 岩叟

translations.literal: Son: Yansou
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yansou

sentences.zh: 岩叟，字孟弼，大節子也。

translations.literal: Yansou, style name Mengbi, was Dajie's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yansou, whose style name was Mengbi, was Zhang Dajie's son.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年進士，調葭州司候判官，再除雄州觀察判官，補尚書省令史，除大理評事，再遷監察御史、同知河東北路轉運使事、中都路都轉運副使、刑部員外郎、忻州刺史，以父憂去官。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the nineteenth year of Dading; appointed judicial assistant of Jia Prefecture, twice made observation commissioner's judge of Xiong Prefecture, filled a clerkship in the Secretariat, made reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, twice promoted to investigating censor, associate director of transport on the Hedong North Circuit, associate director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit, vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, prefect of Xin—he left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the nineteenth year of Dading and served as judicial assistant at Jia Prefecture, twice as observation judge at Xiong Prefecture, then as a Secretariat clerk, reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, investigating censor, associate director of transport on the Hedong North Circuit, associate director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit, vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, and prefect of Xinzhou; he left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 起複大理少卿、河北東西大名等路按察轉運副使，累遷刑部侍郎，兼夔王傅，太常卿兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and surveillance and transport deputy for the Hebei East and West and Daming circuits; he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of punishments, concurrently tutor to the Prince of Kui, grand master of sacrifices concurrently director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he became vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and surveillance and transport deputy for the Hebei East and West and Daming circuits, rose to vice minister of punishments, concurrently tutor to the Prince of Kui, and grand master of sacrifices with concurrent charge of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，朝廷欲塞諸城門以為兵備，集三品官議於尚書省，岩叟曰：「塞門所以受兵，是任城而不任人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an the court wished to block all city gates for military defense; third-rank officials were assembled for discussion at the Secretariat; Yansou said: "Blocking gates is to receive the enemy—it is trusting the walls and not trusting men.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Da'an the court planned to seal the city gates for defense. Third-rank officials met at the Secretariat. Yansou said, "Sealing the gates means receiving the enemy behind walls—it trusts ramparts, not people.

sentences.zh: 莫若遣兵擇將，背城疾戰。」

translations.literal: Better to send out troops, choose generals, and fight with one's back to the wall."
translations.idiomatic: Better to deploy troops, choose commanders, and fight with the city at your back."

sentences.zh: 時議多之。

translations.literal: At the time most in council approved.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials present agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 除鎮西軍節度使，移定國軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army and moved to the Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army, then transferred to the Dingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，改昭義，複移沁南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was changed to Zhaoyi and again moved to Qinnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to Zhaoyi, then again to Qinnan.

sentences.zh: 逾年，按察司言其年老不任邊要，乃致仕，退寓洛陽，卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year the surveillance office reported that he was old and unfit for frontier duties; he then retired, withdrew to Luoyang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the surveillance office reported that he was too old for frontier duty; he retired, settled in Luoyang, and died there.

sentences.zh: 張亨，字彥通，大興漷陰人。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, style name Yantong, was a native of Huyin in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, whose style name was Yantong, came from Huyin in Daxing.

sentences.zh: 登皇統六年進士第，調樊山丞，以廉幹聞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Huangtong and was appointed assistant magistrate of Fanshan, becoming known for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the sixth year of Huangtong and was appointed assistant magistrate of Fanshan, where he became known for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 授弘州軍事判官，曆巨鹿、宜川令。

translations.literal: He was appointed military judge of Hong Prefecture and served successively as magistrate of Julu and Yichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military judge of Hong Prefecture and served in turn as magistrate of Julu and Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，補尚書省令史，除大理司直，累遷尚書左司郎中，授戶部侍郎，移吏部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he filled a clerkship in the Secretariat, was made direct judge of the Court of Judicial Review, was repeatedly promoted to director of the Left Secretariat, appointed vice minister of revenue, and moved to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he took a Secretariat clerkship, became direct judge of the Court of Judicial Review, rose to director of the Left Secretariat, was made vice minister of revenue, and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 擢中都路都轉運使，坐草場使鄧汝霖盜草失舉劾，解職，削一官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit; for failing to impeach the pasture commissioner Deng Rulin, who stole fodder, he was dismissed and demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit, he was dismissed and demoted one rank for failing to impeach the pasture commissioner Deng Rulin, who had stolen fodder.

sentences.zh: 起授戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗問宰臣曰：「御史中丞馬惠迪與張亨人才孰優？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong asked the chief ministers: "Which is superior in talent, Vice Censor-in-Chief Ma Huidi or Zhang Heng?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong asked his chief ministers, "Which man has the greater talent—Vice Censor-in-Chief Ma Huidi or Zhang Heng?"

sentences.zh: 平章政事張汝霖曰：「惠迪為人雖正，於事不敏，亨吏才極高。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Zhang Rulin said: "Huidi is upright in character but not quick in affairs; Heng's administrative talent is extremely high."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Zhang Rulin replied, "Huidi is upright in character but not quick in affairs; Heng's administrative talent is outstanding."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「如汝父浩，于事明敏少有及者，但臨事多徇，若無此過則誠難得之賢相也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "As with your father Hao, in affairs there are few as clear and quick—yet he often bends to expediency; without that fault he would truly be a hard-to-find worthy chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your father Hao was among the clearest and quickest in affairs, yet he often bent to expediency. Without that flaw he would truly have been a rare worthy chancellor."

sentences.zh: 時車駕車巡，費用百出，自遼以東泉貨甚少，計司患其不給，欲輦運以支調度，亨謂：「上京距都四千里，若挽錢而行，是率三而致一也，不獨枉費國用，無乃重勞民力乎。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was touring and expenses were innumerable; east of Liao coin was very scarce, and the accounting office feared shortfall and wished to transport coin by cart to meet disbursements; Heng said: "The Northern Capital is four thousand li from the capital—if coin is hauled there, it is bringing three to deliver one; this not only wastes state funds but surely overburdens the people.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tour was underway and expenses multiplied. East of Liao, currency was scarce; the accounting office feared a shortfall and proposed hauling coin by cart. Heng said, "The Northern Capital is four thousand li from the capital. Hauling coin there means spending three to deliver one—it wastes state funds and surely overburdens the people.

sentences.zh: 不若行會便法，使行旅便於囊橐，國家無轉輸之勞而用自足矣。」

translations.literal: Better to implement the convenience-exchange method so travelers may carry coin in their purses, and the state will be spared transport labor while supplies suffice of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Better to use the convenience-exchange system so travelers can carry value in their purses; the state will avoid transport costs and still have enough on hand."

sentences.zh: 出為絳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army.

sentences.zh: 已而複謂宰臣曰：「漢人三品以上官常少得人，如張亨近令補外，頗為眾議所歸，以朕觀之，無甚過人。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he again told the chief ministers: "Han officials of third rank and above seldom prove worthy; Zhang Heng was recently sent to fill an outside post and was much praised in public opinion, yet in my view he is not greatly above others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he again told his chief ministers, "Han officials of third rank and above seldom prove worthy. Zhang Heng was recently sent outside and drew much public praise, yet as I see it he is not greatly above the rest.

sentences.zh: 小官中豈無才能之士，第未知耳。」

translations.literal: Among minor officials are there not able men? They are simply unknown."
translations.idiomatic: Surely there are able men among lower officials—we simply do not know them yet."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「亨嘗為左司，奏事多有脫略，是亦謬庸人也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Heng once served in the Left Secretariat and in memorializing often omitted details—he too is a blundering mediocrity."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Heng once served in the Left Secretariat and often left gaps in his reports—he too is a muddled mediocrity."

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，初置九路提刑司，時方重其選，上以亨為河東南北路提刑使，兼勸農採訪事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, the nine-circuit chief judicial commissioners were first established and selection was then highly valued; the emperor appointed Heng chief judicial commissioner of the Hedong North and South circuits, concurrently charged with encouraging agriculture and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong succeeded, the court first established chief judicial commissioners for nine circuits and took their selection seriously. Heng was appointed chief judicial commissioner for the Hedong North and South circuits, with concurrent duties to encourage farming and conduct investigations.

sentences.zh: 訪其利病，條為十三事以聞，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: He investigated benefits and harms and memorialized thirteen items; the emperor praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated local abuses and benefits, set forth thirteen recommendations, and the emperor approved them.

sentences.zh: 亨在職每事存大體、略苛細，御史以寬緩不事事劾之，降授蔡州防禦使。

translations.literal: In office Heng always kept to the larger pattern and overlooked petty detail; censors impeached him for leniency and not pursuing every matter, and he was demoted to commissioner of the Caizhou Defense Army.
translations.idiomatic: Heng in office always grasped the larger pattern and overlooked petty detail. Censors impeached him for excessive leniency, and he was demoted to commissioner of the Caizhou Defense Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷南京路轉運使，轉知歸德府事，致仕。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to director of transport on the Nanjing Circuit, then transferred to govern Guide Prefecture, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became director of transport on the Nanjing Circuit, then prefect of Guide, and retired.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Taihe, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taihe at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 亨才識強敏，明達吏事，終始有可稱雲。

translations.literal: Heng's talent and insight were strong and quick, and he was clear in administrative affairs—there was praise for him from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was quick-witted and thoroughly versed in administration; his career from start to finish won praise.

sentences.zh: 韓錫，字難老，其先自析津徙薊之漁陽。

translations.literal: Han Xi, style name Nanlao—his ancestors had moved from Xijin to Yuyang in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xi, whose style name was Nanlao, came from a family that had moved from Xijin to Yuyang in Ji.

sentences.zh: 祖貽願，遼宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yiyuan was Liao commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yiyuan had been Liao commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父秉休，歸朝，領忠正軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Bingxiu submitted to the [Jin] court and held the post of military commissioner of the Zhongzheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bingxiu submitted to the Jin court and served as military commissioner of the Zhongzheng Army.

sentences.zh: 錫以廕補閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Xi entered office by yin privilege as palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Xi entered service through yin privilege as a palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 天會中，南伐，錫從軍掌禮儀，俄以母，老乃就監差。

translations.literal: During Tianhui, in the southern campaign, Xi followed the army in charge of ritual; shortly afterward, because his mother was old, he took a supervisory post.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhui, when the army campaigned south, Xi followed as master of ceremonies. Soon afterward, as his mother had grown old, he took a supervisory assignment.

sentences.zh: 久之，授神銳軍都指揮使，入為宮苑使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed commander of the Shenrui Army and entered the capital as palace park commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed commander of the Shenrui Army and entered the capital as palace park commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天德元年，擢尚書工部員外郎，領燕都營繕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiande he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat and directed repairs in the Yan capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiande he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Works and placed in charge of repairs in the Yan capital.

sentences.zh: 特賜胡礪榜進士及第，四遷尚書戶部侍郎，以母喪解。

translations.literal: He was specially granted jinshi standing on Hu Li's examination list, was promoted four times to vice minister of revenue in the Secretariat, and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted jinshi standing through Hu Li's examination list, rose four times to vice minister of revenue, and left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 旋起復舊職，付金牌一、銀牌十、籍水手于山東。

translations.literal: He was soon recalled to his former post, given one gold tally and ten silver tallies, and registered sailors in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to his former post, given one gold tally and ten silver tallies, and assigned to register sailors in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 時蘇保衡為水軍都統制，趨杭州，俾錫部船三百會廣陵。

translations.literal: At the time Su Baoheng was overall commander of the naval forces and hurried to Hangzhou; Xi was ordered to lead three hundred ships to join at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Su Baoheng was then overall commander of the navy and hurried to Hangzhou; Xi was ordered to lead three hundred ships to rendezvous at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 適保衡敗還，喪船過半，令錫補足之。

translations.literal: Just then Baoheng returned defeated, having lost more than half his ships, and Xi was ordered to make up the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Baoheng soon returned in defeat, having lost more than half his fleet, and Xi was ordered to replace the lost vessels.

sentences.zh: 時水淺，船不得進，海陵遣使急責之，眾稍亡，錫召諸豪諭之曰：「今連保法嚴，逃將安往，縱一身偶脫，其如妻子何？」

translations.literal: The water was shallow and the boats could not advance; Prince Hailing sent envoys to press him urgently; the men began to desert; Xi summoned the local magnates and instructed them: "The mutual-responsibility law is strict—where can deserters flee? Even if one man escapes for a time, what of wife and children?"
translations.idiomatic: The water was too shallow for the boats to advance. Hailing sent urgent envoys to rebuke him, and men began to desert. Xi summoned local leaders and said, "The mutual-responsibility law is strict—where can deserters go? Even if one man slips away, what becomes of his wife and children?"

sentences.zh: 眾悟，亡者稍止。

translations.literal: The crowd understood, and desertions gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The men understood, and desertions gradually stopped.

sentences.zh: 大定改元於遼東，錫奔赴行在，詔複前職。

translations.literal: When the reign title was changed to Dading in Liaodong, Xi hurried to the mobile court and was ordered to restore his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed to Dading in Liaodong, Xi hurried to the mobile court and was ordered back to his former post.

sentences.zh: 明年，授同知河間府事，引見於香閣，誡之曰：「聞皇族居彼者縱甚，卿當以法繩之。」

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed associate prefect of Hejian Prefecture and received audience in the Fragrant Pavilion; he was admonished: "I hear that imperial clansmen living there are very unrestrained—you must restrain them by law."
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made associate prefect of Hejian and received audience in the Fragrant Pavilion. The emperor warned him, "I hear the imperial clansmen there are wildly unrestrained—you must restrain them by law."

sentences.zh: 錫下車宣佈詔言，後無有撓政害民者。

translations.literal: Xi on taking office proclaimed the edict; afterward none obstructed government or harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xi proclaimed the edict as soon as he took office, and afterward no one obstructed government or harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 遷孟州防禦使，累拜絳陽軍節度使，改知濟南府事。

translations.literal: He was moved to commissioner of the Mengzhou Defense Army, was repeatedly appointed military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army, and was changed to prefect of Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to commissioner of the Mengzhou Defense Army, repeatedly served as military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army, and became prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 告老，許之。

translations.literal: He reported old age and was permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement on grounds of age and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Mingchang, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Mingchang at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 鄧儼，字子威，懿州宜民人也。

translations.literal: Deng Yan, style name Ziwei, was a native of Yimin in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan, whose style name was Ziwei, came from Yimin in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 大定中，為左司員外郎、右司郎中，尋轉左司，掌機務者數年。

translations.literal: During Dading he was vice director of the Left Secretariat, director of the Right Secretariat, and soon transferred to the Left Secretariat, handling confidential affairs for several years.
translations.idiomatic: During Dading he served as vice director of the Left Secretariat and director of the Right Secretariat, then moved to the Left Secretariat and handled confidential affairs for several years.

sentences.zh: 有司奏使宋者，世宗命選漢官一人，參知政事梁肅以戶部侍郎王翛、工部侍郎張大節、左司郎中鄧儼對，世宗曰：「王翛、張大節苦無資歷，與左右司官辛苦不同，其命儼往。」

translations.literal: When the authorities memorialized on an envoy to Song, Emperor Shizong ordered selection of one Han official; Participating Councilor Liang Su nominated Vice Minister Wang Xiao of Revenue, Vice Minister Zhang Dajie of Works, and Director Deng Yan of the Left Secretariat; the emperor said: "Wang Xiao and Zhang Dajie truly lack seniority—the toil of Left and Right Secretariat officials is not the same; order Yan to go."
translations.idiomatic: When officials proposed an envoy to Song, Shizong ordered a Han official chosen. Councilor Liang Su named Wang Xiao, Zhang Dajie, and Deng Yan; the emperor said, "Wang Xiao and Zhang Dajie lack senior standing—the work of Left and Right Secretariat officials is not the same. Send Yan."

sentences.zh: 嘗謂宰臣曰：「人言鄧儼用心不正，朕視儼奏事其心識甚明，在太府監心亦向公。」

translations.literal: He once told the chief ministers: "People say Deng Yan's intentions are not upright, but when I see Yan memorialize his mind and judgment are very clear; when he was at the Imperial Treasury his heart was also turned to the public good."
translations.idiomatic: He once told his chief ministers, "People say Deng Yan is not upright, but in his memorials his judgment is very clear, and when he was at the Imperial Treasury he was fair-minded."

sentences.zh: 宰臣因奏儼明事機、有心力，於是擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The chief ministers thereupon memorialized that Yan understood affairs and had drive, and he was promoted to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers then reported that Yan understood affairs and had drive, and he was promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 翌日，複謂宰臣曰：「吏部掌銓選，當得通練人，可置儼於吏部。」

translations.literal: The next day he again told the chief ministers: "The Ministry of Personnel controls selection—it should have a thoroughly practiced man; Yan may be placed in the Ministry of Personnel."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again told his chief ministers, "The Ministry of Personnel controls appointments and needs a thoroughly practiced man—Yan should be placed there."

sentences.zh: 因改命焉。

translations.literal: He was therefore reassigned accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned accordingly.

sentences.zh: 累遷中都路都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of transport for the Zhongdu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 明昌初，為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingchang he became minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Mingchang he became minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書省集百官議，如何使民棄末務本以廣儲蓄。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Secretariat to assemble officials to discuss how to make the people abandon secondary pursuits and return to fundamentals so as to broaden storage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Secretariat to gather officials to discuss how to make the people abandon secondary pursuits, return to fundamentals, and broaden state reserves.

sentences.zh: 儼言：「今之風俗競為侈靡，莫若定立制度，使貴賤、上下、衣冠、車馬、室宇、器用各有等差，裁抑婚姻喪葬過度之禮，罷去鄉社追逐無名之費，用度有節則蓄積日廣矣。」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Present custom competes in extravagance; better to fix institutions so noble and base, high and low, dress, carriages, dwellings, and implements each have gradations, curb excessive marriage and funeral rites, abolish village-community pursuits of nameless expense—if expenditure has measure, accumulation will daily grow."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "Custom now competes in extravagance. Better to fix institutions so that rank, dress, carriages, dwellings, and implements each have proper gradations, curb excessive marriage and funeral rites, and abolish wasteful village festivals—then restrained spending will steadily build reserves."

sentences.zh: 尋知歸德府事，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made prefect of Guide Prefecture, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Guide, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 初，儼致仕複夤緣求進，上問左右：「鄧儼可複用乎？」

translations.literal: Earlier, after Yan retired he again curried favor seeking reappointment; the emperor asked those around him: "Can Deng Yan be used again?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Yan retired he again curried favor seeking reappointment. The emperor asked those around him, "Can Deng Yan be used again?"

sentences.zh: 平章政事完顏守貞曰：「儼有才力，第以謀身為心。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Wanyan Shouzhong said: "Yan has ability, only his heart is set on advancing himself."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Wanyan Shouzhong said, "Yan has ability, but his heart is set on advancing himself."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕亦知之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know that too.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know that as well.

sentences.zh: 然儼可以誰比？」

translations.literal: Yet whom can Yan be compared with?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet whom can Yan be compared with?"

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「臨事則不後於人，但多務自便耳。

translations.literal: Shouzhong said: "In handling affairs he is not behind others, only he is much given to self-convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong said, "In handling affairs he is not behind others, but he is much given to self-convenience.

sentences.zh: 儼前乞致仕，陛下以其頗黠故許之，甚合眾議。

translations.literal: Yan earlier begged to retire; Your Majesty permitted it because he is rather crafty—that accorded well with public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yan earlier begged to retire; Your Majesty permitted it because he is rather crafty—that accorded well with public opinion.

sentences.zh: 今使複列於朝，恐風化從此壞矣。」

translations.literal: If he is now restored to court, I fear custom will from this be corrupted."
translations.idiomatic: If he is now restored to court, I fear public morals will be corrupted from this point on."

sentences.zh: 上然之，遂不復用雲。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, and he was not again employed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Yan was not employed again.

sentences.zh: 巨構，字子成，薊州平谷人。

translations.literal: Ju Gou, style name Zicheng, was a native of Pinggu in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Gou, whose style name was Zicheng, came from Pinggu in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼篤學，年二十登進士第。

translations.literal: From youth he studied earnestly; at twenty he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He studied earnestly from youth and passed the jinshi examination at twenty.

sentences.zh: 由信都丞察廉為石城令，補尚書省令史，授振武軍節度副使。

translations.literal: From assistant magistrate of Xindu he was judged incorrupt and made magistrate of Shicheng, filled a clerkship in the Secretariat, and was appointed deputy military commissioner of the Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: From assistant magistrate of Xindu he was judged incorrupt and made magistrate of Shicheng, took a Secretariat clerkship, and was appointed deputy military commissioner of the Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 改同提舉解鹽司事，以課增入為少府監丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to associate director of the Jie Salt Commission; for increased revenue he entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was made associate director of the Jie Salt Commission and, for increased revenue, entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 再遷知登聞檢院，兼都水少監。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to director of the Petition Review Office, concurrently vice director of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to director of the Petition Review Office and concurrently vice director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 時右司郎中段珪卒，世宗曰：「是人甚明正可用，如巨構每事但委順而已。」

translations.literal: At the time Director Duan Gui of the Right Secretariat died; Emperor Shizong said: "That man was very clear and upright and could be used; as for Ju Gou, in every matter he only complies."
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Gui, director of the Right Secretariat, died, Shizong said, "That man was very clear and upright and could be used; Ju Gou, by contrast, only complies in every matter."

sentences.zh: 二十五年，除南京副留守，上謂宰臣曰：「巨構外淳質而內明悟，第乏剛鯁耳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was made deputy guardian of Nanjing; the emperor told the chief ministers: "Ju Gou is outwardly plain and inwardly perceptive, only lacking firmness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was made deputy guardian of Nanjing. The emperor told his chief ministers, "Ju Gou is outwardly plain and inwardly perceptive, only lacking firmness.

sentences.zh: 佐貳之任貴能與長官辨正，恐此人不能爾。

translations.literal: The duty of a deputy values being able to dispute with the chief— I fear this man cannot do that.
translations.idiomatic: A deputy's duty requires disputing with the chief—I fear Gou cannot do that.

sentences.zh: 若任以長官，必有可稱。」

translations.literal: If given chief responsibility, there would surely be praise."
translations.idiomatic: If given chief responsibility, he would surely prove praiseworthy."

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，擢橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, he was promoted to military commissioner of the Henghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong succeeded, Gou was promoted to military commissioner of the Henghai Army.

sentences.zh: 承安五年致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired in the fifth year of Cheng'an and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in the fifth year of Cheng'an and died.

sentences.zh: 構性寬厚寡言，所治以鎮靜稱，性尤恬退，故人既貴不復往來，先遺以書則裁答寒溫而已。

translations.literal: Gou was by nature generous and sparing of words; his administrations were known for calm; he was especially retiring—when old friends had risen in rank he did not visit again, and if they sent letters first he answered only with conventional greetings.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was generous and sparing of words; his administrations were known for calm. He was especially retiring—when old friends had risen in rank he did not visit again, and if they wrote first he answered only with conventional greetings.

sentences.zh: 大定中，詔與近臣同經營香山行宮及佛舍，其近臣私謂構曰：「公今之德人，我欲舉奏，公行將大任矣。」

translations.literal: During Dading he was ordered with close ministers jointly to build the Xiangshan traveling palace and Buddhist halls; a close minister privately told Gou: "You are a man of virtue today; I wish to memorialize in your praise—you will soon receive great appointment."
translations.idiomatic: During Dading he was ordered with close ministers to build the Xiangshan traveling palace and Buddhist halls. A close minister privately told Gou, "You are a man of virtue today; I wish to memorialize in your praise—you will soon receive great appointment."

sentences.zh: 構辭之。

translations.literal: Gou declined.
translations.idiomatic: Gou declined.

sentences.zh: 以廉慎守法在考功籍，始終無過雲。

translations.literal: For integrity, caution, and observance of law he was on the merit-review rolls and from first to last had no fault.
translations.idiomatic: Listed in the merit-review rolls for integrity, caution, and observance of law, he had no fault from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 賀揚庭

translations.literal: He Yangting
translations.idiomatic: He Yangting

sentences.zh: 賀揚庭，字公叟，曹州濟陰人也。

translations.literal: He Yangting, style name Gongsou, was a native of Jiyin in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Yangting, whose style name was Gongsou, came from Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 登天德三年經義進士第，調範縣主簿兼尉，籍有治聲。

translations.literal: He passed the jingyi jinshi examination in the third year of Tiande and was appointed chief clerk and concurrently bailiff of Fan County; his register showed a reputation for good government.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jingyi jinshi examination in the third year of Tiande and was appointed chief clerk and concurrently bailiff of Fan County, where his record showed a reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 大定十三年，由安肅令補尚書省令史，授沁南軍節度副使，入為監察御史，曆右司都事、戶部員外郎、侍御史、右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dading, from magistrate of Ansu he filled a clerkship in the Secretariat, was appointed deputy military commissioner of the Qinnan Army, entered as investigating censor, and served successively as chief clerk of the Right Secretariat, vice director of revenue, attendant censor, and vice director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Dading, from magistrate of Ansu he took a Secretariat clerkship, became deputy military commissioner of the Qinnan Army, entered as investigating censor, and served as chief clerk of the Right Secretariat, vice director of revenue, attendant censor, and vice director of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世宗喜其剛果，謂揚庭曰：「南人礦直敢為，漢人性奸，臨事多避難。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was pleased with his firmness and told Yangting: "Southerners are blunt and daring; Han nature is crafty and in affairs mostly shuns difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was pleased with his firmness and told Yangting, "Southerners are blunt and daring; Han character is crafty, and in affairs they mostly shun difficulty.

sentences.zh: 異時南人不習詞賦，故中第者少，近年河南、山東人中第者多，殆勝漢人為官。」

translations.literal: Formerly southerners did not study rhapsody and prose, so few passed the examinations; in recent years many from Henan and Shandong have passed— they may surpass Han men in office."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly southerners did not study rhapsody and prose, so few passed the examinations; in recent years many from Henan and Shandong have passed—they may surpass Han men in office."

sentences.zh: 俄以廉能遷戶部郎中，進官二階。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for integrity and ability he was moved to director of the Ministry of Revenue and advanced two ranks in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for integrity and ability, he was made director of the Ministry of Revenue and advanced two ranks.

sentences.zh: 頃之，授左司郎中，改刑部侍郎、山東東路轉運使。

translations.literal: " Before long he was appointed director of the Left Secretariat, then changed to vice minister of punishments and director of transport on the Shandong East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed director of the Left Secretariat, then vice minister of punishments and director of transport on the Shandong East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，初置九路提刑司，驛召赴闕，授山東東西路提刑使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, the nine-circuit chief judicial commissioners were first established; he was summoned by post horse to court and appointed chief judicial commissioner of the Shandong East and West circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong succeeded, the nine-circuit chief judicial commissioners were first established. Yangting was summoned urgently to court and appointed chief judicial commissioner of the Shandong East and West circuits.

sentences.zh: 揚庭性疾惡，纖介不少容。

translations.literal: Yangting hated evil and would not tolerate the slightest fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yangting hated evil and would not tolerate the slightest fault.

sentences.zh: 明昌改元，詔諸路提刑使入見，親問所察事條，至揚庭則斥之曰：「爾何治之煩也。」

translations.literal: When the reign title was changed to Mingchang, an edict ordered chief judicial commissioners of all circuits to enter audience; the emperor personally asked the items they had investigated; when it came to Yangting he rebuked him: "Why is your governance so troublesome?"
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title was changed to Mingchang, chief judicial commissioners of all circuits were ordered to audience; the emperor personally asked what they had investigated. When it came to Yangting he rebuked him: "Why is your governance so troublesome?"

sentences.zh: 明年，下除洺州防禦使，時歲歉民饑，揚庭諭蓄積之家令出所餘以糶之，饑者獲濟，洺人為之立石頌德。

translations.literal: The next year he was demoted to commissioner of the Luozhou Defense Army; that year harvest failed and the people were hungry; Yangting instructed households with stores to sell their surplus grain; the hungry were relieved, and the people of Luo erected a stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was demoted to commissioner of the Luozhou Defense Army. That year the harvest failed and the people were hungry. Yangting urged wealthy households to sell their surplus grain; the hungry were relieved, and the people of Luo erected a stone inscription in his praise.

sentences.zh: 改陝西西路轉運使，表乞致仕，上曰：「揚庭能幹者也，當何如？」

translations.literal: He was changed to director of transport on the Shaanxi West Circuit; he memorialized begging to retire; the emperor said: "Yangting is an able man—what should be done?"
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of transport on the Shaanxi West Circuit and memorialized begging to retire. The emperor said, "Yangting is an able man—what should be done?"

sentences.zh: 右丞劉瑋言其疾，遂許之 。

translations.literal: Vice Director Liu Wei said he was ill, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Liu Wei said he was ill, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十七。

translations.literal: He died aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：裴滿亨以進士選奉禦，能陳唐、虞致治之道于宮庭燕私之地，又能斥中貴梁道兒之奸。

translations.literal: Appreciation: Pei Manheng, chosen through the jinshi examination as palace attendant, was able to set forth the way of Tang and Yu governance in the palace's private leisure, and also could expose the wickedness of the favored attendant Liang Dao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Appreciation: Pei Manheng, chosen through the jinshi examination as palace attendant, could set forth Tang and Yu governance even in the palace's private leisure and expose the favored attendant Liang Dao'er's wickedness.

sentences.zh: 斡勒忠以吏道致身，始終不交權貴。

translations.literal: Wala Zhong rose through the path of clerical administration and from first to last did not associate with the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Wala Zhong rose through clerical administration and never associated with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 世宗自立於遼東，歸者如市，張大節獨守正不赴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong established himself in Liaodong, those who returned were like a market; Zhang Dajie alone upheld integrity and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong established himself in Liaodong, returnees thronged like a market; Zhang Dajie alone upheld integrity and did not go.

sentences.zh: 韓錫出守河間，面諭皇族之居彼者恣睢不道，俾繩以法，佞者必希旨以市權，錫下車宣佈告戒而已。

translations.literal: Han Xi went out to govern Hejian and was face-to-face instructed that imperial clansmen living there were overbearing and lawless and should be restrained by law; flatterers would surely curry favor to trade on power—Xi on taking office only proclaimed the admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xi went out to govern Hejian and was told face to face that imperial clansmen there were overbearing and must be restrained by law. Flatterers would curry favor for power; Xi on taking office only proclaimed the admonition.

sentences.zh: 是皆有識之士，不為富貴所移者也。

translations.literal: These were all men of insight, not shifted by wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: These were all men of insight, not moved by wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 巨構骫骳，賀揚庭骨鯁，大定於二人而屢評南北士習之優劣，亶其然乎。

translations.literal: Ju Gou was compliant, He Yangting was firm— Emperor Dading in these two men repeatedly judged the relative merits of northern and southern scholarly habits; was it not indeed so?
translations.idiomatic: Ju Gou was compliant and He Yangting was firm. Emperor Dading repeatedly judged northern and southern scholarly habits through these two men—was it not indeed so?

sentences.zh: 張亨始以繆庸見薄，晚以論列稱賞，亦砥礪之功歟。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng was at first despised as blundering and mediocre, yet in later years won praise through his policy discussions—was that also the fruit of tempering?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng was at first despised as blundering and mediocre, yet in later years won praise through his policy discussions—was that also the fruit of tempering?

sentences.zh: 鄧儼專務謀身，上下稱黠，致仕又求進用，弗可改也夫。

translations.literal: Deng Yan devoted himself solely to advancing himself; high and low called him crafty; after retirement he again sought reemployment—such a man cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yan devoted himself solely to advancing himself; high and low called him crafty; after retirement he again sought reemployment—such a man cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 閻公貞

translations.literal: Yan Gongzhen
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gongzhen

sentences.zh: 焦旭，字明銳，沃州柏鄉人。

translations.literal: Jiao Xu, style name Mingrui, was a native of Baixiang in Wozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Xu, whose style name was Mingrui, came from Baixiang in Wozhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調安喜主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 再轉大興令，攝左警巡事，以杖親軍百人長，有司議其罪當杖決，世宗曰：「旭親民吏也，若因杖有官人複行杖之，何以行事？

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to magistrate of Daxing and acted as left metropolitan patrol; for beating a hundred-man leader of the imperial guard with a staff, the authorities judged that the crime warranted beating; Emperor Shizong said: "Xu is an official close to the people—if for beating an official one again beats him, how can he conduct affairs?
translations.idiomatic: He was twice transferred to magistrate of Daxing and acted as left metropolitan patrol. For beating a hundred-man leader of the imperial guard with a staff, the authorities judged he should be beaten in turn. Shizong said, "Xu is an official close to the people—if for beating an official he is beaten again, how can he govern?

sentences.zh: 其令收贖。」

translations.literal: Let him redeem the penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Let him redeem the penalty instead."

sentences.zh: 改良鄉令。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to magistrate of Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸春水，見石城、玉田令皆年老不治，謂宰臣曰：「縣令最親民，當得賢才。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the spring waters he saw that the magistrates of Shicheng and Yutian were all old and did not govern; he told the chief ministers: "Magistrates are closest to the people—they should have able men.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the spring waters he saw that the magistrates of Shicheng and Yutian were old and did not govern. He told his chief ministers, "Magistrates are closest to the people and should be able men.

sentences.zh: 畿甸尚如此，天下可知矣。」

translations.literal: Even the capital region is like this—the empire can be known."
translations.idiomatic: Even the capital region is like this—one can imagine the rest of the empire."

sentences.zh: 平章政事石琚薦旭幹能可甄用，上然之，召為右警巡使。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Shi Jue recommended Xu as capable and fit for selection; the emperor approved and summoned him as right metropolitan patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Shi Jue recommended Xu as capable and fit for selection. The emperor approved and summoned him as right metropolitan patrol.

sentences.zh: 旭為人剛果自任，不避權勢。

translations.literal: Xu was by nature firm and self-reliant and did not avoid the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was firm and self-reliant by nature and did not avoid the powerful.

sentences.zh: 初，旭部民訴良，旭以無文據付本主，道逢監察御史訴其事，語涉訛亂，即收付旭，旭釋之不問，為御史所劾，削官兩階，杖百八十，出為大名府推官。

translations.literal: Earlier a subject of his district sued for freedom; Xu, for lack of documentary proof, returned him to his master; on the road he met an investigating censor who sued the matter, his words involving confusion, and Xu was immediately handed over to Xu; Xu released him without inquiry and was impeached by the censor, demoted two ranks, beaten one hundred eighty strokes, and sent out as judicial push officer of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a subject of his district sued for freedom; Xu, lacking documentary proof, returned him to his master. On the road the man met an investigating censor and sued the matter incoherently; Xu was handed the case, released the man without inquiry, was impeached by the censor, demoted two ranks, beaten one hundred eighty strokes, and sent out as judicial push officer of Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋授右三部檢法司正，代韓天和為監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed director of the Right Three Departments Legal Review Office, replacing Han Tianhe as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed director of the Right Three Departments Legal Review Office, replacing Han Tianhe as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時御史台言：「監察糾彈之司，天和諸科出身，難居是職。」

translations.literal: At the time the Censorate said: "The investigating censor is the office of impeachment—Tianhe came up through miscellaneous examinations and finds it hard to hold this post."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Censorate said, "The investigating censor is the office of impeachment—Tianhe came up through miscellaneous examinations and finds it hard to hold this post."

sentences.zh: 上命別舉，中丞李晏薦旭剛正可任，遂授之，而改天和獲鹿令。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered another selection; Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yan recommended Xu as upright and fit for appointment, and he was appointed, while Tianhe was changed to magistrate of Huolu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered another selection. Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yan recommended Xu as upright and fit; Xu was appointed, and Tianhe was made magistrate of Huolu.

sentences.zh: 章宗初即位，太傅克甯、右丞相襄請上出獵，旭劾奏其非，上慰諭之，為罷獵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong first took the throne, Grand Tutor Kening and Right Chancellor Xiang asked the emperor to go hunting; Xu impeached this as improper; the emperor comforted and instructed them and canceled the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong first succeeded, Grand Tutor Kening and Right Chancellor Xiang asked the emperor to go hunting. Xu impeached this as improper; the emperor comforted them and canceled the hunt.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，登聞鼓院初設官，宰執奏司諫郭安民、補闕許安仁及旭皆堪擢用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, when the Petition Drum Court first established offices, the chief ministers memorialized that Remonstrator Guo Anmin, Supplementation Officer Xu Anren, and Xu were all fit for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang, when the Petition Drum Court first established offices, the chief ministers memorialized that Remonstrator Guo Anmin, Supplementation Officer Xu Anren, and Xu were all fit for promotion.

sentences.zh: 改侍御史，四遷都水監，以治河防勞進官一階，授西京路轉運使，卒。

translations.literal: He was changed to attendant censor, was promoted four times to superintendent of waterways, for labor in river defense was advanced one rank in office, was appointed transport commissioner of the Western Capital circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant censor, promoted four times to superintendent of waterways, and advanced one rank for his work on river defenses. He was then appointed transport commissioner of the Western Capital circuit and died in office.

sentences.zh: 旭性警敏，練達時政，與王翛，劉仲洙輩世稱能吏雲。

translations.literal: Xu was by nature alert and keen, thoroughly versed in affairs of the time; together with Wang Xiao, Liu Zhongzhu, and others he was called an able officer of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was quick-witted and thoroughly versed in current affairs. He and Wang Xiao, Liu Zhongzhu, and others were renowned as able administrators of their day.

sentences.zh: 劉仲洙

translations.literal: Liu Zhongzhu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongzhu

sentences.zh: 劉仲洙，字師魯，大興宛平人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongzhu, styled Shilu, was a native of Wanping in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongzhu, styled Shilu, came from Wanping in Daxing.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，登進士第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Dading era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 曆龍門主簿、香河酒稅使，再調深澤令。

translations.literal: He served successively as registrar of Longmen and wine-tax commissioner of Xianghe, then was transferred again as magistrate of Shenze.
translations.idiomatic: He served as registrar of Longmen and wine-tax commissioner of Xianghe, then was reassigned as magistrate of Shenze.

sentences.zh: 縣近滹沱河，時秋成，水忽暴溢，仲洙極力護塞，竟無害。

translations.literal: The county lay near the Hutuo River; at autumn harvest the water suddenly burst forth in flood; Zhongzhu exerted himself to guard and block it, and in the end there was no harm.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay near the Hutuo River. At harvest time the river suddenly flooded, but Zhongzhu threw himself into the dikes and kept the county safe.

sentences.zh: 有盜夜發，居民震驚，仲洙率縣卒生執其一，餘眾遂潰，旦日掩捕皆獲。

translations.literal: Thieves struck by night and the residents were alarmed; Zhongzhu led county soldiers and captured one alive; the rest of the band then dispersed, and at dawn a sweeping arrest took them all.
translations.idiomatic: When thieves raided by night and terrified the populace, Zhongzhu led county troops and captured one alive. The rest fled, and by dawn a sweep had taken them all.

sentences.zh: 尋以廉能進官一階，升河北西路轉運司支度判官，入為刑部主事，六遷右司員外郎，俄轉吏部。

translations.literal: Soon for integrity and ability he was promoted one rank, was made revenue adjutant of the Hebei West Circuit Transport Office, entered service as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, was promoted six times to assistant director in the Right Secretariat, and soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted one rank for integrity and competence, became revenue adjutant on the Hebei West Circuit transport staff, entered the Ministry of Justice as a principal clerk, rose through six posts to assistant director in the Right Secretariat, and soon moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂宰臣曰：「人有言語敏辯而庸常不正者，有語言拙訥而才智通達、存心向正者，如劉仲洙頗以才行見稱，然而口語甚訥也。」

translations.literal: Shizong told the chief ministers: "Some men are quick and eloquent in speech yet mediocre and not upright; others are awkward and slow in speech yet intelligent, capable, and upright in heart. Liu Zhongzhu is much praised for conduct and talent, yet his speech is very halting."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told his chief ministers, "Some men speak fluently yet are mediocre and corrupt; others speak haltingly yet are intelligent, capable, and upright. Liu Zhongzhu is widely praised for talent and character, but he is painfully slow of speech."

sentences.zh: 右丞張汝霖曰：「人之若是者多矣，願陛下深察之。」

translations.literal: Right Vice Chancellor Zhang Rulin said: "There are many such men; I hope Your Majesty will examine them closely."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Chancellor Zhang Rulin said, "There are many such cases. I hope Your Majesty will look into them carefully."

sentences.zh: 二十九年，出為祁州刺史，以六善為教，民化之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he went out as prefect of Qizhou, took the Six Virtues as his teaching, and the people were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was posted as prefect of Qizhou, where he governed through the Six Virtues teaching, and the people were transformed by it.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，除中都、西京等路提刑副使。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong succeeded, he was appointed vice surveillance commissioner of the Central Capital, Western Capital, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong took the throne, he was made vice surveillance commissioner for the Central Capital, Western Capital, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 先是，田玨等以黨罪廢錮者三十余家，仲洙知其冤，上書力辨，帝從之，乃複玨官爵而黨禁遂解。

translations.literal: Previously more than thirty households including Tian Jue had been disfranchised and confined on faction charges; Zhongzhu knew they were wronged, memorialized forcefully in their defense; the emperor assented, restored Jue's office and rank, and the faction ban was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, more than thirty households including Tian Jue had been stripped of office and confined in the Tian Jue party case. Knowing they had been wronged, Zhongzhu memorialized forcefully on their behalf. The emperor agreed, restored Jue's rank and title, and lifted the faction ban.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，授並王傅、兼同知大同府事，尋改平陽，移德州防禦使。
